newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Feb industrial output up 0.55 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Feb industrial output up 0.55 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's industrial output in February rose 0.55 percent compared to February 1996, the economics ministry said on Thursday.
The virtually flat growth in industial output was far below an average forecast of a 7.31 percent rise that resulted from a March 18 Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists.
In that poll, the most cautious economist surveyed expected a year-on-year increase of 5.24 percent, while the most optimistic forecast a 12.8 percent rise.
The finance ministry's chief statistician, Chang Yao-chung, attributed the decline to fewer working days in February compared to Feburary 1996.
Although Taiwan's main annual holiday, the traditional Chinese lunar new year, fell in February in both years, there were only 17.5 working days in February 1997 compared to 19 in February 1996.
The manufacturing index, including metals, machinery, information electronics, chemical and consumer products, rose 2.82 percent in February from the same month in 1996.
Real estate and construction industry output saw a sharp drop, falling 47.57 percent from a year earlier.

But Chang said a year-on-year rise of 7.27 percent in the land area for which construction firms have sought for development permits indicated that the long-sluggish sector would see a clear rebound in the second half of 1997.
"This is the third consecutive month of rise for land area being sought for development. This indicates a recovering property market," Chang said.
